values: Dashboard provides a high-level overview of the personal PDF library. It displays the total number of documents, completed documents and favourite documents, and allows the user to quickly resume recently read documents. The screen also provides navigation to Library, Recent and Favorites, together with global document search.
Include any mockups, diagrams or visual designs relating to these requirements.
Overview of Dashboard loading, navigation and resume-reading activities.
When the user opens Dashboard, the system shall retrieve the document list and display Library Status and Continue Reading data.
Show loading placeholders while data is being retrieved.
Display the application name “Truyenthieu” and subtitle “Personal Library” in the left navigation area.
Display only; no click action is required in this version.
Highlight Dashboard as the active menu item while SCR-01 is displayed.
Only one navigation item may be active at a time.
When the user selects Library, navigate to the Library screen.
Target screen ID shall follow the project screen list.
When the user selects Recent, navigate to the list of recently read documents.
Recent documents are ordered by the latest reading activity.
When the user selects Favorites, navigate to the list of documents where favorite = true.
Favorite state is stored in SQL Server.
Allow the user to search documents by title, author or tag.
Search is case-insensitive. Empty keyword does not start a search.
When the user submits a keyword, navigate to Library and display the filtered result.
The keyword is transferred to Library as a search condition.
Display the Settings icon at the top-right of the screen.
If Settings is outside the current scope, the icon shall be hidden or disabled.
Display the total number of documents in the library.
Display the number of documents whose readingStatus is COMPLETED.
Do not calculate from progress percentage if readingStatus is available.
Display the number of documents whose favorite value is true.
Label should be “Favourite Books” or “Favorite Books” consistently.
Display a limited list of documents that have been started but not completed, ordered by most recent reading activity.
Recommended display limit: 2 items. Requires a reliable recent-reading timestamp; otherwise use updatedAt as a temporary assumption.
Display the title of each recent document.
Long titles are truncated according to responsive rules.
Display the author of each recent document.
Display “Unknown author” only if author becomes optional.
Display a short summary of each recent document.
If summary is empty, hide the summary area rather than displaying blank text.
Calculate and display reading progress as lastReadPage / totalPages × 100.
If totalPages is null or zero, display progress as unavailable.
Display the last read page and total pages in the format “Page X of Y”.
Page number must be within 1 and totalPages.
Display a visual progress bar corresponding to the calculated reading percentage.
Clamp the displayed value to the range 0–100%.
When selected, open the PDF Reader for the document at lastReadPage.
If an offline copy exists, prefer IndexedDB; otherwise use the configured source.
When selected, navigate to the Recent screen and display the complete recent-document list.
Button is hidden when there are no recent documents.
When the library has no documents, display an empty-state message and a link/button to add a document.
Status totals are displayed as zero.
When there are no recently read documents, display a message indicating that no reading activity exists.
Do not display empty document cards.
When dashboard data cannot be loaded, display an error message and provide a Retry action.
The screen shall not display stale counts as current values.
On desktop, display the sidebar, three status cards in one row and full-width recent-document cards.
Reference design width is desktop 1440 px or greater.
On mobile, collapse navigation, stack status cards and display recent-document cards in one column without horizontal page scrolling.
Touch targets should be large enough for mobile operation.
Display the application version in the footer.
Display whether the application is currently online or offline.
Connection mode reflects browser connectivity; document offline availability is managed separately per document.
